lines.text: In 1914, a couple in Idaho mailed their five year old daughter
to her grandma's house.
With the stamps stuck right on her coat.
See, the post office had just started delivering packages,
and May's parents wanted her to visit grandma,
seventy-three miles away.
But a train ticket wasn't cheap.
So her dad walked her into the post office
and asked how much it costs to mail a kid.
The clerk checked the rules,
and nothing said he couldn't.
May weighed forty-eight and a half pounds,
just under the fifty pound limit.
So on went fifty-three cents in stamps,
and she rode the train in the mail car,
with her mom's cousin, who happened to be the mail clerk.
He walked her right up to grandma's front door.
Soon after, the post office banned mailing people.
Which is why today, you can still mail baby chicks,
but not your little sister.
